punchline: A Boston hospital cut soda sales without a single lecture. It just put water next to the cash register.
thirty_sec: A doctor at Massachusetts General Hospital wanted staff and visitors to drink healthier, but she didn't try to persuade anyone. She simply stocked water in the fridges by the cash registers, which had held only soda, and set out baskets of water at food stations. Soda stayed on sale. Within three months, soda sales fell about 11 percent and water rose about 26 percent. Where things sit mattered more than what people intended.
question: If someone rearranged your kitchen or desk overnight, which of your habits do you think would change first?
